ownerStatement: Approved by repeat98 on 17 Nov 2026 in the session that tested big module sets on his MKII: "approved" to FM Synth 0.1.4-experimental after reading that its only change is the CPU price of 6, the measurement behind it, the unit trial of the package (seven tracks admitted, the eighth refused) and what stays untested. The author, Tim Hastie, gave the owner his OK for optimizations verbally (owner's word, 13 and 14 Nov 2026); that it covers naming the price was the session's judgement, made when the owner said to answer that question for him.
reason: 0.1.4 changes only FM Synth's CPU price: "cpuPrice": 6 in its machine-ports.json entry, which machine_ports.py writes as reserved[0] of the generated mw_machine descriptor, and resources.cpuPrice in octamod.module.json. The module's code is 0.1.3's; in its folder only release-notes.json, the manifest and Markdown changed, and the USB package differs from 0.1.3's in that one byte. The price is what one playing track adds to the frame interrupt, measured with 0.1.3 on the owner's MKII (development twin 945cc074 of base 0.7.7, 17 Nov 2026): 36.8 % with a trig on every step of one FM Synth track against 32.2 % without, 4.6 points, priced 6. The base's CPU budget (45 % a Part) then admits seven FM Synth tracks where its default price of 12 admitted three. The UI and pages are 0.1.2's, so its captures are retained. Waived for this exact source, as for 0.1.3: chords, glide, MIDI, legacy FMSYNTH samples, GLIDE on sample tracks and track 1's LFO 3 on a unit, listening by ear, Part/project reload and power cycles, the card build on a unit, chip worst-case cycles and complete memory bounds.
